rows.reasoning: My initial rating was too high. While the head is well-formed, the body's geometry is not just 'soft,' it's lumpy, poorly defined, and lacks the crispness one would expect even from stylized 'origami folds.' The different views reveal that the 'feathers' are just indistinct blobs that melt into each other, which would look cheap and unfinished in a real application. The consensus from other judges made me re-evaluate this from a technical perspective, where the execution is clearly poor.

My previous score was completely wrong. After reviewing the group feedback, I examined the views more closely and it is now clear that this is not a single, coherent 3D object. The shape and volume of the body, as well as the point where the neck joins the body, change between views. This is not a rotation of a single asset; it's a collection of four similar but distinct models. This is a catastrophic failure for a 3D asset, as it would appear to morph during user interaction.

While the asset consistently depicts the animal 'swan,' it fails to consistently depict 'a single 3D object.' For any interactive use case, an object that changes its fundamental shape when viewed from a different angle is deeply misleading to the user and breaks the illusion of reality. This failure of object permanence is a critical semantic flaw. My initial rating overlooked this, but the group feedback correctly identified it as a major issue.

The realization that the asset is structurally inconsistent and geometrically messy completely shatters its aesthetic appeal. What I initially saw as a 'charming' and 'graceful' style, I now see as a technically broken and unconvincing render. The 'artistic' quality is an illusion masking fundamental flaws. It doesn't look elegant; it looks broken.

I was too generous in my interpretation of 'soft.' The prompt's core textural request was 'origami folds,' which implies crisp planes and defined creases. This asset has none of that. The body is simply lumpy and blob-like. It completely fails to capture the 'origami' concept, even a soft version of it. The asset is a white swan, but it does not have the specified feather texture.
